headline: Lebanese Forces ministers boycott cabinet session over Hezbollah explosives case referral delay
dek: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] At least four Lebanese Forces ministers boycotted Thursday's cabinet session, protesting the state's delay in referring Hezbollah's explosives-trafficking case to the Judicial Council. Hezbollah has acknowledged hundreds of kilograms of explosives seized at Dahr al-Baidar…
sources: Jerusalem Post (officials' statements + Asharq Al-Awsat), corroborated by This Is Beirut and Naharnet pre-session reporting
fault_line: Sovereignty or civil war? Should Beirut refer Hezbollah's own acknowledged explosives shipment to the top security court, or does forcing the case risk the civil war Berri warns about?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] At least four Lebanese Forces ministers boycotted Thursday's cabinet session, protesting the state's delay in referring Hezbollah's explosives-trafficking case to the Judicial Council. Hezbollah has acknowledged hundreds of kilograms of explosives seized at Dahr al-Baidar (early October) belonged to the group, claiming they were intended for use against Israel. Investigators identified seven suspects incl. the two men in the explosives vehicle, still in custody; Judge Claude Ghanem (government commissioner to the Military Court) was expected to receive Army Intelligence + ISF findings Thursday, paving the way for charges. This Is Beirut adds the LF ministers had also withdrawn from the Oct 15 session over the same refusal, and that Thursday's session agenda omitted the file (waste management instead).
sections.what_verified: Jerusalem Post (T3) + Naharnet (T3) pre-session reporting (cabinet meets 3pm Thursday; Justice Ministry referral request on agenda; Berri advising postponement). Asharq Al-Awsat (T3, STATE-SA) via JPost for the Ghanem/findings line. This Is Beirut (no declared tier) corroborates the boycott motive but is NOT counted.
sections.what_disputed: Hezbollah's position: shipment intended for use against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, denies assassination/domestic-use allegations, and demanded the shipment's return (rejected). Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri warned referral could ignite civil war and urged postponement pending completed investigations; cabinet previously routed the case via the military judiciary with Judicial Council referral left as an unspecified future possibility. Nidaa al-Watan (via Naharnet) reported a majority would likely vote FOR referral if a vote occurred - outcome of Thursday's session itself not yet reported.
sections.why_matters: Hezbollah admits the explosives are theirs - and Beirut still won't send the case to court: four ministers walk out
